title: Coefficient presentation identifies the bounded finite-Tor generator predicates
statement: Let B be a finite discrete commutative topological ring, X a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], and eR a monoidal isomorphism from the constant lifted B-ring on profinite sets to its continuous-function condensed ring [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant]. Put A=ULift B. Let P consist of bounded constructible etale coefficient-model complexes with a finite coefficient-model Tor interval [def-pe-etale-constructible-module, det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian], and Q the analogous pro-etale coefficient-model predicate. Use the explicit model realizations E and G [lem-ctf-finite-comparison-model-realization]. Then the replete image P.map D(E) is exactly the ordinary etale bounded constructible finite-Tor predicate, and Q.map D(G) is exactly the predicate that the specified internal realization has bounded constant-model constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [lem-ctf-finite-comparison-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. This concerns coefficient presentations separately on each site and does not assert any etale/pro-etale comparison.

source.place: opening paragraph: coefficient identification before invoking finite-Tor comparison

proof.text: Use the specified exact coefficient-model and small-site equivalences. Express local finite constant modules using a covering sieve and transport these same sieves, modules and constant-sheaf isomorphisms across the equivalences and slice restrictions. On the pro-etale site identify the terminal covering sieve with scheme covers through the weakly etale slice equivalences and the public finite-models-over lemma.

Globalize affine-local finite stratifications on the qcqs scheme with the generic refinement argument. Apply the local constant-module comparisons on every stratum, keeping the actual pullback morphisms.

For a finite module over the finite coefficient ring, use a finite free cokernel presentation. The common internal/ordinary encoding preserves the regular module, finite sums and cokernels, so its constant internal module is finitely presented. Construct its constant internal presheaf explicitly, with componentwise scalar action, and then sheafify. The action comparison gives the ordinary constant sheaf without unfolding identity scalar restriction. Transport it along eR inverse. The monoidal constant-sheaf pullback comparison identifies its point pullback with the specified scheme encoding, with explicit transport between the canonical and monoidally induced ring structures.

The common encoding commutes with the specified normalized scheme pullbacks. Thus each ordinary finite local constant model supplies the same finite point model after encoding. Conversely the existing finite-constant-local-model theorem makes finite point models locally finitely presented, so the existing constructible encoding theorem recovers ordinary constructibility. Use the same finite stratification in both directions.

Identify the literal internal realization with the common encoding using the sheafification adjunction. Its inverse is the section-module equivalence followed by restriction along the specified constant-ring isomorphism and constant scalar restriction. The section action and sheafification-unit equations identify these scalar actions exactly.

Build the strong monoidal structure with Mathlib's CoreMonoidal.mk' constructor from the normalized tensor and unit isomorphisms and coherence of the proved public section-tensor-comparison theorem. First prove existence of the coherent ordinary monoidal structure in a private lemma, then select it through that small interface. Only existence of the strong monoidal structure is needed for finite-Tor transport. Compose it with normalized ring-isomorphism tensor transport and constant scalar restriction. Equivalence preserves and reflects flatness, so the coefficient-model flat-complex criterion and the derived tensor transport identify the same finite Tor intervals.

Exact equivalences commute with homology and preserve and reflect zero objects, so they preserve the finite cohomological vanishing intervals. Apply the constructibility comparisons to homology. Finally essential surjectivity and closure under isomorphisms identify the two replete images.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteComparisonPresentation (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (eR : Sheaf.sheafifyRingPresheaf.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (coherentTopology Profinite.{u})
      ((Functor.const Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ).obj (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B))) ≅
        Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) [IsMonHom eR.hom] :
    let A := ULift.{u + 1} B
    letI : IsNoetherianRing A := inferInstance
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (ConstantCompletion.Mod (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A)) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (ConstantCompletion.Mod (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A)) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    let P : ObjectProperty (ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A)) :=
      fun K ↦ Scheme.IsCoefficientBoundedConstructibleEtale.{u, u + 1} X A K ∧
        ∃ a b : ℤ, HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude _ K a b
    let Q : ObjectProperty (ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant
        (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u + 1} X) A)) :=
      fun K ↦ coefficientBoundedConstructibleProEtale.{u, u + 1} X A K ∧
        Scheme.HasFiniteCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude.{u, u + 1} X A K
    P.map (finiteComparisonEtaleModelRealization X A).mapDerivedCategory =
        finiteComparisonEtaleGenerators B X ∧
    Q.map (finiteComparisonProEtaleModelRealization X A).mapDerivedCategory =
        finiteComparisonProEtaleGenerators B eR X
